title: Readability Repair Bench
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: MicroSims
Diagram Readability
Accessibility
Information Design
Flowcharts
description: A p5.js MicroSim in which learners critique a deliberately cluttered 20-node flowchart against seven readability standards (text size, contrast, label length, size, color use, interaction, layout), name each flaw by clicking it, and repair the diagram with five fixes whose effects depend on their order.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Diagram readability standards and the order of repairs
learningObjectives: The learner will critique a cluttered diagram against the readability standards and repair it by applying fixes in order of effect.
prerequisites: The readability standards table in Chapter 8

accessibility.notes: describe() summary for screen readers; repairs are native HTML buttons; status lights also show a text status (met, violated, not checked)

controls.label: Click a flaw
controls.purpose: Names the violated standard and lights its checklist item

controls.label: Enlarge fonts
controls.purpose: Raise node text from 9 px to 16 px

controls.label: Shorten labels
controls.purpose: Replace long labels with 2-5 word labels and move the detail into hover text

controls.label: Fix contrast
controls.purpose: Replace pale yellow text with near-black text

controls.label: Split into two
controls.purpose: Split the 20-node diagram into two diagrams of 8 and 12 nodes

controls.label: Add symbols
controls.purpose: Pair each meaning color with a symbol and a legend

controls.label: Show Before / Show After
controls.purpose: Compare the original and the repaired diagram

controls.label: Show part 1 / 2
controls.purpose: Switch between the two diagrams after the split

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Hit-region flaw finder plus rubric checklist with status lights
keyQuestions: Which standard does each flaw violate?
Which repairs satisfy more than one standard?
Why does enlarging fonts before shortening labels gain less?
commonMisconceptions: Bigger text always makes a diagram more readable (not if labels no longer fit)
Color alone is enough to mark categories (some readers cannot distinguish the colors)
Shortening labels loses information (the detail moves into hover text)
assessmentOpportunities: Number of distinct standards the learner finds by clicking before repairing
Whether the first two repairs are the two largest-effect fixes

simulation.modelType: Rule-based rubric (standards as a function of applied repairs)
equations: Text size = fonts; Contrast = contrast; Label length = shorten; Size = split; Color use = symbols
Interaction = shorten (detail moves into hover text, notes overlay removed)
Layout = split AND NOT (fonts AND NOT shorten)
assumptions: Contrast is judged for the pale-text nodes only
limitations: The standards are the generator guides' recommendations, not measured results
Hover text is shown in a message box rather than a floating tooltip
